summary: Castaway Island Seaplane Base (CST) serves the private Castaway Island resort, located in the Mamanuca Islands archipelago off the western coast of Viti Levu, Fiji. As a dedicated seaplane facility, it provides the primary access route for resort guests arriving from Nadi, offering spectacular aerial views of Fiji's tropical reef systems and turquoise lagoons. The base exemplifies Fiji's well-established seaplane network that connects remote island resorts to the mainland.
faqs:
Q: How do I get to Castaway Island Seaplane Base?
A: Most travelers fly into Nadi International Airport on Viti Levu and transfer to a scenic seaplane flight, which takes approximately 10-15 minutes to reach the island.

Q: Which airlines operate seaplane services to this base?
A: Seaplane transfers to the Mamanuca Islands are typically operated by carriers such as Fiji Seaplane and Pacific Island Air from Denarau Marina or Nadi.

Q: Is the seaplane base open to non-resort guests?
A: The seaplane base primarily serves guests of Castaway Island Resort; day visitors should arrange excursions through the resort or approved tour operators.

Q: What is the best time of year to visit?
A: The dry season from May to October offers the calmest seas and clearest skies, ideal for seaplane operations and water activities.
transport_tips: Seaplane baggage allowances are strictly limited to soft bags, typically around 15-20 kg per guest, so pack light and leave hard suitcases at your Nadi hotel. Confirm your seaplane transfer at least 24 hours in advance through the resort, as departures are weather-dependent and grouped by resort destination. Upon arrival, a resort boat transfer from the seaplane dock takes guests directly to the main island reception.
local_tip: Request a window seat on the left side of the seaplane for the best views of the Mamanuca reef chain and surrounding coral formations during the approach to Castaway Island.
